newsitem.title: EGYPT: Death of peace process possible - Egyptian official.
newsitem.headline: Death of peace process possible - Egyptian official.

text.p: A senior political adviser to Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said on Wednesday the total collapse of the Middle East peace process was a possibility.
"A nightmare scenario would be the death of the peace process... It is a possibility," said Usama el-Baz.
"Consequences will be bleak for everybody," he told the Foreign Press Association in Cairo.
"If the peace process is interrupted for a long time this would amount to a death."
Baz was answering a question about possible scenarios after Arab foreign ministers decided on Monday to freeze contacts with Israel and reactivate an economic boycott of the Jewish state.
He said the Arabs had not yet decided what course of action they would take to implement the resolution.
"The Arabs are not jumping into the opportunity to boycott or isolate Israel. They have not shaped yet the mechanism for the implementation of that resolution," he said.

"The Arabs will consider through contact and other measures what degree of boycott... (and) it is our earnest hope that a change in the Israeli thinking... and policy happens before the implementation of the resolution."
Israel has angered Arabs by insisting on going ahead with a housing project on Jabal Abu Ghneim, or Hor Homa, in the disputed city of Jerusalem.
Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa also set out the incompatible Arab position.

"To save the peace process needs political statesmanship and courage. The practices and steps that have been taken in Jerusalem will have to be rolled back. This is the starting-point for any effort to save the process," he said.
Moussa was speaking after talks on the Middle East crisis with Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo, who is on a regional tour as president of the European Union council.
